hook: Your brain's threat system was built for a world where the danger lasted seconds. You're running it in a world where the threat is an email that arrived at 11pm.
topic: Evolutionary mismatch — why the amygdala misfires in modern life
body:
**The amygdala evolved in a world where threats were physical, immediate, and brief.**

A predator. A fall. A confrontation that ended one way or another. The threat lasted seconds or minutes — and then it was resolved. The stress response fired, served its purpose, and the system returned to baseline.

The threats your brain encounters now don't resolve that quickly. An unread message. A performance review you're dreading. A relationship that feels uncertain. These are threats that persist — sometimes for days. And your amygdala responds to them the same way it would respond to something physical and immediate. It keeps the alarm running.

There was no evolutionary pressure to develop an off switch for chronic, unresolvable social threat. Because that kind of threat didn't exist.

So the system isn't broken. It's running perfectly — in the wrong environment.

Understanding that changes how you relate to the thoughts. The spiral isn't proof that something is seriously wrong with you. It's proof that you have a very well-calibrated threat system living in a world it wasn't designed for.

That's a problem worth solving with the right tools. Not self-criticism.

Guide is in my bio.
